liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **He's Gone** (1 review): The band mentions PigPen during the song [9]
- **Box Of Rain** (1 review): Bass, piano and guitar trade licks beautifully, and Phil and Donna sing it on key [8]
- **China Cat Sunflower** (1 review): The crowd went wild when the band began the China Cat intro [11]
- **Loose Lucy** (1 review): A slower, rawer version of the song than usual [18]
- **Truckin'** (1 other source): A Nobody's Fault But Mine jam occurs within Truckin' [1]

## Setlist highlights

- **The Race Is On**: back after 204 archived shows (870 days) [19]

## The recordings

- **gd1973-03-19.141298.sbd.miller.patched.flac2496** (recommended): soundboard; 29 songs; 204 min; rated 3.8/5 by 5 [1]
- **gd1973-03-19.sonyecm.moskal.97417.flac16**: source not stated; 28 songs; 207 min; rated 4.8/5 by 5 [3]. Said about its sound: Warm-sounding audience recording that evokes standing at the back of the Coliseum; Levels fluctuate throughout, and there are dead-air gaps in several songs [3][17]
- **gd73-03-19.sbd.elliot.9987.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 13 songs; 118 min; rated 3.5/5 by 6 [5]. Said about its sound: Playback speed sounds too fast, making Bobby and Jerry's voices high-pitched like cartoon chipmunks; Checked against a tuned guitar, pitch is slightly off A=440 but not dramatically, and singers don't sound sped up; Playback speed is correct, the tape doesn't wobble, and instrument and vocal levels are near perfect [7][10][18]
- **gd1973-03-19.partial.aud.danh.97506.flac16**: audience recording; 5 songs; 31 min; rated 3/5 by 2 [6]

## Around the show

- Reviewer attended three Coliseum shows that March and found this Monday night the mellowest of them [8]
- Fans skipped school with parental permission and queued all day outside before getting in [9]
- Third night of a three-show Coliseum run; Jerry Jeff Walker opened solo, then NRPS played a short set [11]
- Fans waited in line all day amid a party atmosphere, then rushed in and got a spot in front of Jerry [11]
- The taper was caught during the show, but this recording omits the confrontation [13]
- Midshow, a band member pointed at the taper; a crew member cut the mic cord and took his tapes [6]
- The taper kept only this tape and the NRPS opening set [6]
- The band played plenty of material from the Europe 72 era [9]
- Judged better than the other audience recording in circulation, though it contains only a few songs [12]
- At the time, this was the only recording of the whole show on the Internet Archive [16]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1973-03-19.141298.sbd.miller.patched.flac2496**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: flac24/96 Recording Info: SBD > Master Reels > Dat (16-bit/44.1k) > upsampled to 24-bit/96k; Mastering Info:WAV > Samplitude Pro X3 Suite > FLAC/24; Master… [1]. Also: Two sets of masters were combined to make the show complete [1]
- **gd1973-03-19.sonyecm.moskal.97417.flac16**: taped by Gerry Moskal; transferred by Gerry Moskal; source: Sony Stereo ECM x 2 -->SONY TCD126 [3]. Also: Taped and shared by a taper named Gerry [3]
- **gd73-03-19.sbd.elliot.9987.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [5]
- **gd1973-03-19.partial.aud.danh.97506.flac16**: taped by Dan H.; transferred by Dan McDonald; source: Unknown Mic, Unknown Cassette recorder (mono) Location: Slightly too close to stage [6]. Also: Dan H. taped near the stage using Adam G.'s microphone [6]
